title: "From" value changed in list pane and preview pane after pulling from Gmail
creator: tsweeney1
content:
I'm boggled by this one. I use Thunderbird 128.2.0esr (64-bit) on Fedora and Gnome. I use it as my mail interface and my POP server is Gmail.

Earlier this week, when I pulled up the list of emails in my inbox, I noticed that emails from GitHub were all "From" one apparently random person. If I click on the email and look at the mail in the preview pane, it too has the incorrect "From" value.

However, if I reply to or forward the email, it will have the correct "From" address.

What's stranger, is I also get emails from Jira and other bots. They two have the same issue but with another person. For instance, all of my emails from GitHub now come from "John Smith". All my Jira emails come from "Elizabeth Doe (Jira)". The people they are coming from are people I receive those types of emails from, but not every single email. I've rebooted, and still the same problem, and still the same wrong people in the From field for GitHub, Jira, and others.

Any ideas?

title: Recent disfunctional changes to Thunderbird
creator: coso.poha
content: I see that Thunderbird has added another feature that makes Thunderbird less functional. First a single click to access Address Book now requires three keys to be depressed; Ctrl, Shift, and b. And this earlier change made it impossible to view incoming mail when accessing Address Book. Second, the change made yesterday requires that only one address can be added to an email at a time. When two or more address are highlighted and dragged to BCC, TO, or CC the user is forced into "Attach". Then the only thing that appears in "Attached" is as lot of gibberish and some personal information about only one of the addresses. I'm wondering just how many are no longer using Thunderbird after these changes? Oh, seems the most logical next change to make is to cease allowing an address to be "dragged" into a slot and require that the address be typed, key by key, into an "TO" slot. Hummm. Could a pattern be noted about using digital information? One of my credit unions made some online changes that make banking on line much, much more difficult. This long time "contributor" is now looking for some other email (and internet?) provider. I do hope that y'all make your product(s) more user friendly, rather than user difficult. DWG PS It took me two or three minutes to access this method of communicating with Mozilla. Y'all sure make it difficult for your users to communicate with you.

title: Thunderbird is slow to respond to ISP server and email messages have too much info added when I forward them.
creator: jvm11
content:
Best Buy installed a new hard drive with additional storage capacity on my computer. A lot of stuff got wiped out and had to be re-installed, including Thunderbird. Now, Thunderbird is slow to respond to the server and even simple reply messages can take a minute or longer to send. It takes a long time to get messages, send, etc. What can I do to increase speed? My ISP tells me I have 45 MB of speed [soon to be 300mb] and that something is slowing down the email process, not them. Also, when I forward a message Thunderbird sends all the coded info with the messages that confuses the receipient. For example, if I send a political cartoon, some will delete the message because the cartoon is on the very bottom of the message and all the sending material is first and he thinks the message is a gag of some sort. Messages used to just show the sender and receipient(s) names and topic, not all the unnecessary detail involved in the message itself. 

Can you please me with these issues, as I am so frustrated that I am exploring using Gmail or Outlook instead.

Thanks. Jim Maciej jvm1@windstream.net
